'''Wreaken Mining Rig Field Tests''' is a pair of linked Community Goals in ''Elite Dangerous'', opened by Wreaken Corporation and [[Vodel]] at '''Metz Enterprise''' in the '''Ega''' system. One goal uses familiar asteroid laser mining as a comparison point. The other puts the [[Rhino]] [[Surface Recon Vehicles|SRV]] and Wreaken's deployable [[Surface Mining|surface-mining]] rigs through a large public field test.<ref name="frontier-cg">[https://www.elitedangerous.com/community/goals Community goals], Frontier Developments. Accessed 2026-09-05.</ref><ref name="galnet-tests">[https://www.elitedangerous.com/news/galnet/wreaken-calls-for-surface-mining-support-tests Wreaken Calls for Surface Mining Support Tests], GalNet, Frontier Developments, 3 September 3312. Accessed 2026-09-05.</ref>

Both goals run from the same station, but they do not track the same cargo or the same mining method. During the opening weekend, several metals sold at unusually high event-enhanced prices at Metz Enterprise. Gold, Palladium and Silver were particularly important to ordinary commodity traders because they could be purchased elsewhere and resold at Metz, while Iridium belonged to the Rhino/surface-mining side of the field tests. That market activity was separate from actually contributing mined cargo to a Community Goal.

== Event background ==

Wreaken has been developing deployable mining equipment for planetary work: rigs that can be set up on the surface, extract resources, and feed into a refinery module. Vodel's Rhino is the vehicle built to carry that idea into the field. GalNet described the Rhino as a large, heavily armoured SRV from Vodel, a Core Dynamics subsidiary, with deployable mining rigs and a refinery module fitted as standard for planetside mining.<ref name="galnet-rhino">[https://www.elitedangerous.com/news/galnet/vodel-reveals-new-srv-rhino Vodel Reveals New SRV Rhino], GalNet, Frontier Developments, 3 September 3312. Accessed 2026-09-05.</ref>

The Ega trials are where that technology stops being a showroom feature and starts being tested by pilots at scale. Dr. Ben Curtis, Wreaken's Chief Geologist, described the work as a way to test the rig's mining-laser technology and learn which materials it can extract from different planetary body types.<ref name="galnet-tests" /> Earlier GalNet coverage tied the project to Wreaken research into surface extraction, deployable drills, refinery modules, and surface scanning for planetary mining sites.<ref name="galnet-research">[https://www.elitedangerous.com/news/galnet/research-sheds-new-light-on-industrial-mining Research Sheds New Light on Industrial Mining], GalNet, Frontier Developments, 24 August 3312. Accessed 2026-09-05.</ref>

The asteroid-mining goal gives Wreaken a baseline. By asking laser miners to deliver conventional mined commodities at the same time, the company can compare established asteroid yields against the new surface-mining loop. For the details of deploying the Rhino, locating deposits, extracting resources, and recovering the rig, see [[Surface Mining with the Rhino]].

== The two Community Goals ==

Metz Enterprise hosts two separate Community Goals. Pilots who want to take part need to dock there and register for the goal they intend to support; joining one does not automatically join the other. The rewards are listed the same way for both, but the targets, accepted cargo, mining methods, and price multipliers differ.<ref name="frontier-cg" />

=== Wreaken Calls for Mining Support to Test New Rig ===

'''Wreaken Calls for Mining Support to Test New Rig''' is the conventional mining side of the trial. Wreaken is asking pilots to laser-mine asteroids so the company can compare normal asteroid yields with the new surface-mining system.<ref name="frontier-cg" />

To contribute, register for this goal at Metz Enterprise, mine qualifying asteroid commodities with laser mining, return to Metz, and sell the cargo through the commodity market. Frontier's active Community Goal data listed a target of '''35,000,000 tonnes''' and a '''6x price multiplier''' for commodities sold as part of this initiative.<ref name="frontier-cg" />

The asteroid goal accepts:

{| class="wikitable" style="width:100%;"
! Asteroid-mining CG commodities
|-
| Platinum, Palladium, Gold, Silver, Bertrandite, Indite, Gallite, Coltan, Uraninite, Lepidolite, Cobalt, Rutile, Water, Painite, Osmium, Praseodymium, Bromellite, Samarium
|}

Live progress and contribution brackets change as more pilots take part. The in-game panel and live trackers such as Inara are the best places to check current percentile thresholds while the goal is active.<ref name="inara-cg">[https://inara.cz/elite/communitygoals/ Community goals], Inara. Accessed 2026-09-05.</ref>

=== Wreaken Calls for Surface Mining Support to Test New Rig ===

'''Wreaken Calls for Surface Mining Support to Test New Rig''' is the Rhino side of the event. This goal is built around Wreaken's deployable surface-mining rig rather than ordinary asteroid mining. After registering at Metz Enterprise, participating pilots sell raw or refined surface-mined materials to the station market.<ref name="frontier-cg" />

Frontier's active Community Goal data listed a target of '''10,000,000 tonnes''' and an '''8x price multiplier''' for materials sold as part of this surface-mining initiative.<ref name="frontier-cg" />

The surface-mining goal accepts:

{| class="wikitable" style="width:100%;"
! Surface-mining CG commodities
|-
| Iridium, Helium, Helium-3, Bastnasite, Deuterium, Thortveitite, Quartz Pyroxenite, Olivine, Periclase Dunite, Sapphire, Diamond, Ruby, Magnesite
|}

These materials are tied to the Rhino and deployable-rig loop, not laser mining in asteroid rings. Commanders unfamiliar with the new system can find the full deployment, extraction, refining, and recovery process in [[Surface Mining with the Rhino]].

== How to participate ==

Start by travelling to '''Ega''' and docking at '''Metz Enterprise'''. Inara listed Metz as a Coriolis starport with large pads, a commodity market, shipyard, outfitting, repair, refuel, rearm, and other major station services, approximately 5,392 Ls from the arrival point.<ref name="inara-metz" />

Once docked, open the Community Goal panel and register for whichever trial you want to support. If you plan to support both, join both separately. From there the loop is straightforward: collect the correct cargo by the method required by that goal, bring it back to Metz Enterprise, and sell it through the commodity market.

=== Mining contribution vs ordinary trading ===

The easy mistake in this event is treating every sale at Metz as Community Goal progress. It is not that simple.

A valid CG contribution requires registration first, and the cargo has to satisfy the rules of the relevant goal. The asteroid goal calls for laser asteroid-mined commodities. The surface goal calls for surface-mined materials from the Rhino/deployable-rig loop.<ref name="frontier-cg" />

Ordinary trade is different. During the opening weekend, purchased Gold, Palladium, Silver, Cobalt, Praseodymium and other normally tradable metals could be bought elsewhere and resold at Metz at event-enhanced prices. That created the metals trading rush, but those tonnes were not mined by the commander and did not advance the asteroid-mining goal. Iridium belonged to the Rhino/surface-mining side and should not be treated as equivalent ordinary station-to-Metz arbitrage. The same station market handled both kinds of sale, so the profit could look similar even when the CG contribution result was not. Event price does not equal Community Goal contribution.

== Rewards ==

Both goals list the same minimum participation rewards. Frontier's active Community Goal page states that pilots who register at least one contribution are eligible for:<ref name="frontier-cg" />

Contribution brackets move as more pilots take part, so current thresholds are best checked in-game or through a live tracker such as Inara while the event is running.<ref name="inara-cg" />

== Event duration and status ==

GalNet announced the field tests on 3 September 3312 and directed independent pilots to register at Metz Enterprise in Ega.<ref name="galnet-tests" /> Frontier's active Community Goal data published an expiry of '''10 September 2026 at 10:00 UTC''' for both goals, while some public tracker data around the event has shown conflicting timers and stale start-date wording.<ref name="frontier-cg" />

Because of that mismatch, the safest live reference is the countdown shown in the in-game Community Goal panel. The event is ongoing as of the 7 September 2026 review for this article.

== Market effects ==

The field tests have had a much bigger effect on Ega than the mining objectives alone. During the opening weekend, Wreaken's boosted purchase prices turned Metz Enterprise into an unusually lucrative commodity market, with several metals and other accepted CG commodities showing prices far outside their normal trading range.<ref name="inara-metz-market">[https://inara.cz/elite/station-market/19179/ Metz Enterprise - market], Inara. Accessed 2026-09-05.</ref>

The opening-weekend effect came from the Community Goal pricing itself. Frontier's opening-weekend data gave the asteroid-mining goal a 6x multiplier and the surface-mining goal an 8x multiplier for commodities sold as part of the initiatives.<ref name="frontier-cg" /> The metals did not all behave identically in ordinary trade: Gold, Palladium and Silver were the metals whose extreme multipliers were subsequently reduced, while other associated metals retained event-enhanced pricing in the September 7 observation below.

=== Event-enhanced metals ===

The opening-weekend market surge affected multiple commodities in the game's metal category. The metals associated with the Wreaken field tests and showing event-enhanced pricing were Cobalt, Gold, Iridium, Osmium, Palladium, Platinum, Praseodymium, Samarium and Silver. Iridium belonged to the Rhino/surface-mining side; the other listed metals were associated with the asteroid-mining Community Goal where applicable. They were not all equally useful for ordinary station-to-Metz arbitrage, since some were primarily or exclusively obtained through mining while others could be sourced through ordinary commodity markets.

The following September 7 figures were observed directly in-game at Metz Enterprise by CMDR Sythan.<ref name="sythan-metals">Direct in-game observation by CMDR Sythan while docked at Metz Enterprise in Ega on 7 September 2026.</ref> They document the broader event-enhanced market and should not be read as a promise that every metal offered the same arbitrage opportunity:

Palladium was one of the clearest numerical examples of the wider opening-weekend metals surge. On 5 September 2026, Inara showed Metz Enterprise buying Palladium for '''302,136 Cr/t''' with '''999,999 t''' of displayed demand.<ref name="inara-palladium">[https://inara.cz/elite/commodity/45/ Palladium - commodity], Inara. Accessed 2026-09-05.</ref> That price is an event-driven snapshot, not Palladium's normal value. A direct in-game observation by CMDR Sythan while docked at Metz Enterprise on 7 September 2026 recorded Palladium at '''75,534 Cr/t''', with '''999,999 t''' of displayed demand and a displayed Galactic Average of approximately '''25,180 Cr/t'''. Compared with the 5 September price, that was a reduction of '''226,602 Cr/t''' or '''75%'''. This records the change for Palladium specifically; it does not establish that every event-enhanced commodity price has ended.

At the same time, Inara's Palladium page listed a trade route from Black Moon Terminus buying at '''47,872 Cr/t''' and selling at Metz Enterprise for '''302,136 Cr/t'''. That left more than 254,000 credits of gross margin on every tonne hauled to Ega.<ref name="inara-palladium" />

{| class="wikitable"
! Item !! Example value
|-
| Source buy price || 47,872 Cr/t
|-
| Metz sell price || 302,136 Cr/t
|-
| Gross spread || 254,264 Cr/t
|-
| 720 t cargo example || 183,070,080 Cr gross spread before expenses and delays
|-
| 784 t cargo example || 199,342,976 Cr gross spread before expenses and delays
|}

Those figures explain why Ega drew so much attention during the opening-weekend metals trading rush, but they are historical snapshots. Prices, supply, and route quality can move quickly, and the real return depends on cargo capacity, travel time, supercruise distance, traffic, interdictions, market data age, and whether the cargo is being moved directly or through carrier logistics.

=== September 7 multiplier change ===

On 7 September, Frontier reduced the extreme event multipliers specifically affecting Gold, Palladium and Silver: Gold fell from 6x to 1.5x, Palladium from 6x to 1.5x, and Silver from 6x to 2x. This brought the extraordinary opening-weekend ordinary-market arbitrage rush to an end without ending event-enhanced pricing for every metal. The September 7 observations above show that Cobalt, Iridium, Osmium, Platinum, Praseodymium and Samarium still had unusually high Metz prices, while the broader Community Goals remained active.

Palladium provides the clearest comparison. The 5 September example used 302,136 Cr/t at Metz and a source price of 47,872 Cr/t, producing the historical 254,264 Cr/t gross spread shown above. Using the separately observed source price around 48,678 Cr/t, the opening-weekend comparison was approximately 253,000 Cr/t, while the 7 September Palladium price produced approximately 26,856 Cr/t before expenses. The historical margins describe 5 September conditions and should not be treated as currently available returns.

=== Fleet Carrier trading ===

During the opening-weekend metals trading rush, [[Fleet Carrier|Fleet Carriers]] amplified the same trade dramatically. Instead of moving one shipload from the source to Ega, a carrier owner could stage tens of thousands of tonnes near a cheap Palladium market, jump the entire stockpile to Ega, and unload it into Metz Enterprise while the extreme event price remained favourable.

Using the observed 5 September 2026 Palladium prices above, a carrier operation moving 20,000 tonnes would have looked like this:

{| class="wikitable"
! Calculation !! Value
|-
| Destination price || 302,136 Cr/t
|-
| Source price || 47,872 Cr/t
|-
| Gross spread per tonne || 254,264 Cr/t
|-
| Cargo moved || 20,000 t
|-
| Gross market spread || 5,085,280,000 Cr
|}

That was gross market spread, not guaranteed profit. Loading time, available carrier capacity, Tritium, carrier services, price movement, and any margin paid to other haulers still came out of the operation.

=== PTN and player-operated logistics ===

Player groups reacted to the opening-weekend spread as well. The Pilots Trade Network, for example, was visible in Inara market data around Ega through carriers and trade listings tied to Palladium movement.<ref name="inara-palladium" /> The practical idea was simple: a carrier operator acquired cargo in bulk, moved it close to the high-price market, and paid haulers to shuttle the final loads between the carrier and Metz Enterprise.

The large historical spread left room for both sides to earn credits when the numbers lined up. That activity was player logistics, not an official part of the Community Goal, and EDFM is not affiliated with PTN. Unloading bought cargo from a carrier was ordinary trade unless the cargo also satisfied the actual CG contribution rules.

=== Solo trading ===

A Fleet Carrier or PTN job was not required to participate in the opening-weekend metals surge. If Palladium, Gold, Silver or another normally tradable metal was available cheaply enough elsewhere, a pilot could buy it, fly directly to Metz Enterprise, and sell into the elevated market.

Those routes depended entirely on the temporary live numbers. The historical figures here should not be used as a current route guide: bought cargo could produce ordinary trade profit during the surge, but it did not count as mined Community Goal contribution.

== Why this event matters ==

Even without the extraordinary trade profits, the Wreaken Mining Rig Field Tests are an important moment for the Rhino. They put the deployable mining-rig system into large-scale public use and place the new surface-mining loop directly beside the asteroid mining players have used for years.

For several days during the opening weekend, Ega was also the centre of an extraordinary metals trading and Fleet Carrier logistics boom. The event remains a live comparison between old and new mining methods, a stress test for the Rhino's surface-extraction gameplay, and a good example of how Community Goal pricing can reshape player behaviour. The response around Metz Enterprise — mined deliveries, direct arbitrage, Fleet Carrier hauling, and player-run logistics — is part of the event's history as much as the final contribution totals will be.
